questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question:
Consider the following GI-tagged products and their states:
1. Lakadong Turmeric - Meghalaya
2. Darjeeling Tea - West Bengal
3. Banarasi Sarees - Uttar Pradesh
4. Mysore Silk - Tamil Nadu
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - Mysore Silk is from KARNATAKA (Mysuru), not Tamil Nadu. Kanchipuram Silk is from Tamil Nadu. Lakadong Turmeric from Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya has highest curcumin content (7-12%) among all turmeric varieties globally. Darjeeling Tea was India's first GI tag (2004-05).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question:
With reference to GI Tags, consider:
1. Tirupati Laddu received a GI tag
2. Alphonso Mango (Hapus) from Ratnagiri has a GI tag
3. Kashmir Saffron has a GI tag
4. A product can have GI tags from multiple states simultaneously
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - a GI tag is linked to a SPECIFIC geographical region. The same product cannot get GI from multiple states simultaneously (that would defeat the purpose). Tirupati Laddu (2009, AP), Alphonso Mango (Ratnagiri/Sindhudurg, Maharashtra), Kashmir Saffron (J&K, 2020 - known for longer stigma and dark color).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question:
Consider the following recently GI-tagged products:
1. Judima Rice Wine - Assam (first beverage from NE India to get GI)
2. Mithila Makhana - Bihar
3. Chhena Poda - Odisha
4. Tandur Red Gram - Telangana
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Judima (traditional rice wine of Dimasa tribe, Assam) was NE India's first GI-tagged beverage (2021). Mithila Makhana (fox nut, Bihar - 2022). Chhena Poda (baked cheese dessert, Odisha - 2023). Tandur Red Gram (Telangana - known for distinctive taste due to black cotton soil). These recent GI tags are highly exam-relevant.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: Which of the following statements about GI Tags in India is INCORRECT?
options: GI registration is valid for 10 years and renewable
Any producer in the registered region can use the GI tag
GI is registered under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is INCORRECT. GI-tagged products CAN be exported (in fact, GI helps in international markets by establishing authenticity and premium pricing). Darjeeling Tea, Basmati Rice, Alphonso Mango are all exported with GI protection. GI even provides protection under WTO's TRIPS agreement internationally.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question:
Consider the following GI-tagged handicrafts:
1. Pashmina - Ladakh/J&K
2. Pochampally Ikat - Telangana
3. Channapatna Toys - Karnataka
4. Blue Pottery - Rajasthan
5. Aranmula Kannadi (metal mirror) - Kerala
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correctly matched with their states. Pashmina (from Changthangi goats of Ladakh). Pochampally Ikat (Nalgonda district, Telangana - tie-dye weaving). Channapatna Toys (lacquerware toys, Ramanagara district, Karnataka). Blue Pottery (Jaipur, Rajasthan - Turko-Persian origin, no clay used). Aranmula Kannadi (unique metal alloy mirrors, only place in world - Aranmula, Kerala).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question:
With reference to GI tags for agricultural products:
1. Naga Mircha (Bhut Jolokia/Ghost Pepper) - Nagaland
2. Shahi Litchi - Bihar
3. Banaganapalle Mangoes - Andhra Pradesh
4. Coorg Green Cardamom - Maharashtra
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - Coorg (Kodagu) is in KARNATAKA, not Maharashtra. Coorg is famous for coffee and spices (cardamom, pepper). Naga Mircha/King Chilli (Scoville 1 million+, one of world's hottest). Shahi Litchi (Muzaffarpur, Bihar). Banaganapalle Mango (Kurnool, AP - known since Mughal era).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
With reference to India's space reforms (2020 onwards):
1. IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre) was created in 2020
2. NSIL (NewSpace India Limited) handles ISRO's commercial activities
3. Private companies can now use ISRO facilities on a rental basis
4. India's space economy target is $50 billion by 2030
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - India's space economy target is around $13 billion by 2025 (currently ~$8 billion). The $50 billion figure is aspirational but not an official government target for 2030. Global space economy is ~$400 billion. IN-SPACe provides single-window clearance. NSIL (2019) commercializes PSLV/GSLV launches and transfers tech to industry. ISRO shares facilities with private players.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Consider the following Indian space startups and their achievements:
1. Skyroot Aerospace - Suborbital launch (Vikram-S)
2. Agnikul Cosmos - 3D-printed rocket engine test from Sriharikota
3. Pixxel - Earth observation satellite constellation
4. Dhruva Space - India's first private satellite in orbit
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Skyroot (Hyderabad): Vikram-S suborbital (Nov 2022). Agnikul (Chennai): tested Agnilet engine and launched from Sriharikota's private launchpad (India's first). Pixxel (Bengaluru): hyperspectral earth observation satellites (launched via ISRO/SpaceX). Dhruva Space (Hyderabad): Thybolt satellites (India's first private satellites in orbit, 2022 via PSLV). India has 190+ registered space startups.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
With reference to India's satellite navigation system NavIC (IRNSS):
1. It provides coverage over India and 1,500 km beyond its borders
2. It uses a constellation of 7 satellites
3. It provides two services: Standard Positioning Service and Restricted Service
4. Its accuracy is better than GPS over the Indian region
questions.explanation: All correct. NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation): 7 satellites (3 in GEO + 4 in GSO orbits). Coverage: India + 1,500 km (regional, not global like GPS). Two services: SPS (civilian, 5m accuracy) and RS (military/authorized, encrypted). Over India, NavIC provides better accuracy than GPS because satellites are positioned specifically for the Indian region. Made mandatory in smartphones sold in India.
